message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most celebrated American composers—across classical, popular, and contemporary genres—whose work has had a lasting impact both in the U.S. and worldwide:

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Classical/Popular crossover | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical | *Appalachian Spring*, *Fanfare for the Common Man*, *Rodeo* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Showtune | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film score | *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalist | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalist | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains*, *Electric Counterpoint* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | *Adagio for Strings*, *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Early 20th‑century | *The Unanswered Question*, *Concord Sonata* |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | March music | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Washington Post” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Broadway & symphonic | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (born 1930) | Musical theatre | *Sweeney Todd*, *Into the Woods*, *Company* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** (not American) – *N/A* | *N/A* |

*(Note: The last row is a placeholder; Beethoven is not an American composer.)*

These figures span a wide range of styles—from early American classical pioneers to modern film composers—and each has left a distinct mark on the musical landscape.
